summary: All 19 units (8 modules) were read in full and every MCQ, numeric and theory item was worked independently before comparing with the key. No wrong answer keys, no MCQ with a second defensible option, and no safety problems were found; lesson tables and statements (rib types, diaphragm attachments and levels, lung/pleura surface levels, coronary territories, mediastinal divisions, inguinal canal, peritoneal classification, renal relations and ureteric constrictions, aortic/IVC branches and tributaries, GI arterial territories, portal anastomoses, pelvic and perineal anatomy, pudendal nerve course) match standard Year 1 anatomy. The recurring weaknesses are low-value filler numeric items (trivial counting or subtraction of lesson values, some with invented physiological figures) and a few small wording or consistency slips, all minor. Confidence is good but this is an AI review only: the course still needs a subject-matter expert (anatomist or clinician) before clinical reliance, and valve surface-projection wording in particular should be checked against the department's prescribed text.

issues.problem: Valve table gives the tricuspid valve projection as 'Behind the lower sternum, approximately opposite the left 4th-5th intercostal spaces'. The tricuspid orifice is usually described as behind the sternum in the midline or right half at the 4th-5th spaces; 'left' conflicts with the common description and with the 'lower sternum' wording. Unverified against the course's prescribed text.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'behind the sternum (midline/right half) at the level of the 4th-5th intercostal spaces', or cite the prescribed text. Keep the left lower sternal border as the auscultation point.

issues.problem: Stem fixes the tricuspid auscultation point at 'the left 5th intercostal space' (6 cm below the pulmonary point) but the lesson table and summary give 'left lower sternal border, usually 4th or 5th intercostal space'. Answer 6 depends on the 5th space only.
issues.suggestedFix: Word the stem as 'taking the tricuspid point at the 5th intercostal space' or recast it as a surface-anatomy counting question without implying a single fixed space.

issues.problem: 'How many intercostal spaces inferior to the sternal angle is the 4th intercostal space?' Key is 3, counting the 2nd space as the first below the angle. A natural offset reading (4th is two spaces below the 2nd) gives 2. The stem does spell out the counting, but the question wording invites the other answer.
issues.suggestedFix: Ask instead 'How many intercostal spaces are encountered, counting the 2nd and the 4th, from the sternal angle down to the 4th?' or ask for the rib/space number reached after moving down two spaces.

issues.problem: Stem uses a canal length of 5.0 cm and a 3 cm vertical rise between rings; the lesson states the canal is 'about 4 cm long' and the deep ring sits only a little above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament, so a 3 cm vertical drop is anatomically implausible. The item is pure Pythagoras with no anatomical content.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the lesson's 4 cm length with plausible components, or replace with a question on deep ring position relative to the inferior epigastric vessels.

issues.problem: Theory question requires the boundaries of the inguinal (Hesselbach) triangle, but the lesson only mentions the triangle in passing and never states its boundaries. Likewise the objective 'contents of the inguinal canal' is covered only as 'spermatic cord' without listing the cord's constituents (vas deferens, testicular artery, pampiniform plexus, cremasteric/genital branch, etc.).
issues.suggestedFix: Add the triangle boundaries (lateral border of rectus, inferior epigastric vessels, inguinal ligament) and a short list of spermatic cord contents to the lesson.

issues.problem: q003, q006 and q009 are three near-identical subtraction questions on oesophageal distances (40-23, 27-15, 27-23) with no anatomical reasoning beyond recalling the lesson table.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep one, replace the others with questions on oesophageal relations (e.g. structure crossing at T4/T5) or the foregut/midgut duodenal boundary.

issues.problem: Stem states 'the superior mesenteric artery list has 5' branch groups, but the lesson table names six (inferior pancreaticoduodenal, jejunal, ileal, ileocolic, right colic, middle colic). The 'branch groups' total of 11 is an arbitrary count with no learning value.
issues.suggestedFix: Delete or replace with a question asking which named arteries supply the appendix or the proximal transverse colon.

issues.problem: Unit title and objectives mention the suprarenal glands but the lesson only notes their fascial position. Relations, arterial supply and venous drainage are absent. Q006 (ellipsoid volume with pi = 3.14) is geometry unrelated to the objectives.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a short suprarenal paragraph (position, three arterial sources, left vs right venous drainage) or drop the suprarenal wording; replace q006 with an anatomical question.

issues.problem: Branch table omits the median sacral artery (the unpaired posterior branch), although q001 option b lists it as 'unpaired' without the lesson ever introducing it. Q006, q007 and q008 are counting items (16 arteries, 8 lumbar arteries, 5 segmental levels) that test arithmetic of table entries, not anatomy.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the median sacral artery to the table and replace the counting questions with identification or relation questions (e.g. left renal vein relation to SMA/aorta).

issues.problem: Table lists the middle rectal artery as supplying the 'Middle and inferior rectum', which blurs the territory of the inferior rectal artery (anal canal below the pectinate line, from the internal pudendal). The prostate row also uses the outdated term 'urogenital diaphragm' while the perineum unit uses 'perineal membrane'. The uterus row gives no position (anteverted/anteflexed) although the objective asks for position. Q010 uses an invented 120 mL/min flow split.
issues.suggestedFix: Say the middle rectal supplies the lower rectum (anastomosing with superior and inferior rectal arteries); use 'perineal membrane/deep perineal pouch'; add uterine version/flexion; replace q010 with a branch-identification question.

issues.problem: Two mechanical formulas (disc fraction h_disc/(h_disc+h_bodies) and F = PA) are introduced and tested in q004, q007 and q010 with invented disc heights and a 0.50 MPa nucleus pressure. They are not in the unit objectives and the 'disc fraction' formula is not a standard anatomical measure.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove or clearly label as optional biomechanics; add questions on regional vertebral features, the anterior/posterior longitudinal ligaments or the traversing versus exiting root instead.

issues.problem: Objective asks to relate occlusion of a specific coronary artery to affected myocardium; the lesson works through only the LAD, with the RCA assessed in q010 and the circumflex never. Q003 and q008 are percentage arithmetic on invented sample sizes (160 and 50 hearts).
issues.suggestedFix: Add a circumflex and RCA occlusion worked example (including SA/AV nodal branch involvement) and replace the percentage items with territory questions.

issues.problem: Objective 'hilar structures of the right and left lungs' is covered only as an unordered list of root contents. The usual arrangement (pulmonary artery superior on the left; right superior lobar bronchus above the artery; veins anterior and inferior) is not taught.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a short hilum arrangement table for each lung.
